stem: Victoria is a 3-year-old girl with a history of two intensive care admissions for asthma exacerbations. She is currently well controlled on fluticasone. Which of the following is an ongoing aim of asthma management?

options.text: To eliminate all respiratory symptoms permanently
To maintain the best possible lung function
To avoid the need for any inhaled medication
To use the highest possible steroid dose at all times

explanation: The ongoing aims of asthma management include minimising symptoms, maintaining the best possible lung function, identifying and avoiding triggers where possible, and minimising adverse effects of treatment. Among the options, maintaining the best possible lung function is a core ongoing aim.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part B

rationale: The original item was multiple-answer. It has been rewritten into a single-best-answer question with one clearly correct option.

optionExplanations.A: Asthma control aims to reduce symptoms, not guarantee permanent elimination.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Maintaining the best possible lung function is an ongoing aim of asthma management.
optionExplanations.C: The goal is not to avoid all medication, but to use the minimum effective treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Management aims to minimise medication side effects, not maximise steroid exposure.

Which of the following are the on-going aims of asthma management? Please note that more than one answer may be correct.

Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Case 1

Victoria is a 3 year old girl with a history of two admissions to the intensive care unit with asthma exacerbations. You are seeing her for the first time. She is currently taking fluticasone (Flixotide) 500 µg three times daily (tds).
